newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Woman fights to exhume Argentine populist leader.
newsitem.headline: Woman fights to exhume Argentine populist leader.

text.p: A woman who wants the late populist leader Juan Domingo Peron exhumed to prove she is his daughter is suing the lawyer for Peron's third wife for libel, her attorney said on Wednesday.

Martha Holgado, 62, has won a court order to have Peron's embalmed body exhumed for DNA tests to support her claim to be a love-child from one of his secret romances in the early 1930s. She says her real name is Lucia Virginia Peron.

Her lawyer Eduardo Barcesat said he had filed a writ against Humberto Linares, the attorney for Maria Estela Martinez de Peron -- known as Isabel -- "for libel, because he described Martha Holgado as a defrauder."
Isabel Peron, who became president when Peron died in office in 1974 but was toppled by a military coup in 1976, does not want Peron's tomb in La Chacarita cemetery opened.
Barcesat said Linares accused Holgado in a writ of "defrauding" her brother in an inheritance suit.
He said other alleged attempts to block the exhumation included a demand that DNA tests be carried out on Holgado's legal parents despite the fact they were cremated in 1975.
"If he were so sure she is not the daughter, he should let us carry out the test tomorrow so he can sue her if the test is negative," Barcesat told Reuters.
Holgado, who clearly resembles Peron, says he and her mother were lovers in 1932 during his first marriage, but she did not learn he was her father until she was 19.
She disagrees with Peron's relatives that he was made sterile by an accident in 1913. None of his three wives, including the legendary Evita, bore him any children.
Peron ruled Argentina from 1946-55 and from 1973-74.
